conviction_note: H1 was pre-released on 10-15 (OP 1,023m against a 548m plan) and the stock sold that upgrade (-2.76% on the day) and has since given all of it back. The print now turns on one decision: does the company raise the full year it explicitly held on 10-15? Holding it implies H2 OP down 25% YoY. Its record (no FY change at any print in four years; FY25's changes came on standalone dates) makes a hold the likely case, and a raise the positive tail, which would also force a dividend rise under the 50%+ payout floor. Against that sit a crowded margin long (15.5x) and a name that sells its beats. The findings sum to +0.7. The scaled number is smaller, p_up 53 x abs 3.5 = +0.21, because the likely outcome is a hold, which the market already saw on 10-15.

For the FY decision: company FY plan OP 2,070m / ordinary 2,565m / net 1,736m / EPS 99.32 / DPS 54 (Q1 短信, https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260729/140120260728500767.pdf). findings.finding: The H1 upgrade (OP 1,023m vs 548m plan, +87%; Q2 standalone OP ~536m vs Q1 487m and 375m a year ago) was filed on 10-15 with the full year explicitly held at OP 2,070m. A held FY implies H2 OP of 1,047m against 1,396m last H2 (-25% YoY), so today's FY decision is the live item. The company has made no FY change at an H1 print in FY23 through FY26 (kabutan shows FY25 revisions only on 2024-08-20 and 2025-02-20), so a hold is the base case. If it does raise (e.g. H2 held: FY OP ~2,545m, net ~2,020m, EPS ~115), the stated >=50% payout floor makes the 54-yen dividend fall to ~47% payout and implies a raise to >=58 yen.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-10-15 H1 upgrade with FY held: -2.76% on the day (spiked to 1,393 intraday, closed 1,338). 2025-10-15 H1 downgrade with FY held: +5.25%. 2025-04-25 FY print with buyback and dividend raise: +17.9% on the day, +28% over two days. 2026-04-27 flat initial guide: -4.73%. FY25 mid-year FY revisions came on non-print dates.
findings.why_not_priced: The H1 number is priced, and so is the FY hold of 10-15: the stock sold that day and is back at its pre-revision level. What is not priced is a FY raise at this print. A market expecting one would have held the 10-15 gain (it is 5% below the 10-14 close), and the PER on the company plan (13.1x) shows no re-rating. The positive tail is underpriced if the company abandons its habit. The hold, the likely case, is already in the price, hence the small expected value.

The FY plan and Q1 figures are from https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260729/140120260728500767.pdf. The revision record is from https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=9932.

baseline_tension: The baseline leans slightly negative (priced_lean -0.61, from the margin overhang), and the run-up is flat after the post-revision giveback. The strongest positive the release could carry is a FY raise with the dividend rise the payout floor would force; I looked for it, and the company's record says it is the less likely outcome. That leaves the findings mildly positive on the tail and the scaled number near zero.
